answer: A sybil-resistant economy can make identity costly to fake by tying each agent to a long-lived, non-transferable stake that accrues only through verified work. A newcomer must deposit a violet bond into a contract that locks for many epochs; the bond is slashed if the agent is caught colluding. A farm cannot share one stake across many aliases because the terrace of work history it builds is unique per identity, and an oasis of shared custody shows up in the audit trail. A haven of clones without distinct work history gains no weight.
